shots.loi: Could Spurs' Kawhi Leonard defend
the Great Wall of China against
Genghis Khan? In 2016, Kawhi won
his second straight Defensive Player of the Year,
averaged 1 .8 steals,
and helped the Spurs win 67 games.
They called him the Claw. Meanwhile, Genghis Khan invaded northern China in 1211. His Mongol army mastered horseback archery, flanking attacks,
and fake retreats that lured enemies into traps.
But there's one problem.
A fake retreat is basically
a pump fake, and
Kawhi doesn't bite on pump fakes.
The Great Wall was tall, but
it had absolutely zero lateral quickness.
So Genghis attacks left, Kawhi slides left. He attacks right, Kawhi slides right. The entire army gets locked up.
Kawhi doesn't even smile.
Therefore, 2016 Kawhi Leonard would
successfully defend the Great Wall of China and
hold the entire Mongol empire to
zero points
on 0 for 1 attempted invasions.
